answer_text: Ethanol, C2H5OH, is a colourless liquid that reacts with sodium metal to release hydrogen and form sodium ethoxide: 2C2H5OH + 2Na -> 2C2H5ONa + H2. When heated with concentrated sulphuric acid at 443 K it loses water and gives ethene, so sulphuric acid acts as a dehydrating agent. Hot alkaline potassium permanganate oxidises ethanol to ethanoic acid, and the purple colour of KMnO4 is discharged.
